verses.1: The words that Jehovah spoke to Babylon, to the land of Kashdim, through the prophet Jeremiah.
verses.2: Speak in the nations, and let them hear! Let them be filled with joy. Do not be sad; say that Babylon has been captured. She is proud and arrogant. Her pride has caused her downfall.
verses.3: For a foreign nation rose up against her; they destroyed her land completely. No man or animal could live there anymore.
verses.4: In those days, and at that time, the Lord will say, “The children of Israel and the children of Judah shall come together. They will walk together, and they will weep together. And they will worship the Lord their God.”
verses.5: The Israelites will ask for guidance from Him. They will come before Him and be united with God in a covenant that will last forever, without ever being broken.
verses.6: My people were like lost sheep. They wandered up the mountains, trying to find their way back to the valley. They forgot about their path.
verses.7: All their offerings were eaten by them, and their enemies said, “We will not worship under the shadow of His righteousness.” May Jehovah be holy and worthy of praise, just as their ancestors were.
verses.8: They came out of Babylon and from the land of Keshdim. They stood before the throne.
verses.9: For behold, I am from a city that lies above Babylon. There are many nations from the land of Assyria who plan to attack it. They will try to take control over it, but they won’t succeed. They will be like a foolish leader who doesn’t know what he’s doing.
verses.10: And it shall be like a vineyard for all those who seek its fruit. All of its fruits will be multiplied, says the LORD.
verses.11: For you will rejoice, for you will be overjoyed when I restore my inheritance to you. You will understand that it’s like a baby being born, and you will dance with joy.
verses.12: Your ancestors lived in those lands that were separated from the Mediterranean Sea and Arabia.
verses.13: May the LORD not rest in this place; let it remain empty. All that has happened in Babylon shall be destroyed, and all its ruins will be scattered everywhere.
verses.14: They took control of Babylon and all its surrounding areas. They went there with their hands raised in worship. But do not be afraid of the flames, for it is God’s fault that there has been sin.
verses.15: They praised her around her. Her hands were given to her. Her arms fell down. Her clothes were destroyed. For Jehovah has avenged her. He has taken revenge on her for what she did.
verses.16: They cut down the branches from the trees in Babylon, and they pluck the grapes at the time of harvest, before the autumn season begins. Then each person will go back to his own people, and each person will return to his own land.
verses.17: Then Israel was scattered across the lands. The first king who ruled over them was Asher. And the next king was Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon.
verses.18: Therefore, as the Lord, the God of Israel, says: “I will punish Babylon’s king and his land, just as I punished Assyria’s king.”
verses.19: And I restored Israel to its former state. The Carmel and Bashan were also restored, as well as Mount Efraim and Gilad. Their souls will be at peace.
verses.20: In those days and at that time, the Lord will demand retribution for the sins of Israel. There will be no forgiveness for the sins of Judah. But those who repent will be forgiven.
verses.21: Over the land, there will be destruction. It will be turned into a place of ruin and desolation. But Jehovah will act according to all that you have been commanded.
verses.22: The sound of war is heard in the land, and great destruction follows.
verses.23: How was it that the land was destroyed and broken apart? How did Samael become king over the nations?
verses.24: I have sought you everywhere, but you were not found. You were lost in Babylon, and you did not know that you were being sought. But now, you are found, because of the Lord’s strength.
verses.25: The LORD opened His storehouse, and all His wrath was revealed. For it is the work of the LORD God, His army, on the earth, in all places.
verses.26: From afar, they opened their eyes and saw her. They were like bees; they rushed towards her. But she remained silent, without saying anything.
verses.27: All her sheep came down to the valley. They were in danger, for it was time for their punishment to come.
verses.28: The voices of vengeance and anger come from the land of Babylon, to proclaim in Zion the vengeance of our God. It is the vengeance of His temple.
verses.29: Hear, Babylon! Many voices will be heard from all directions. The gates of heaven will be closed around her. There will be no peace for her; everything she has done will be punished. For she has gone against the LORD and against Israel’s holiness.
verses.30: Therefore, they will fall in their own fields and across their own lands. All those who were involved in that battle will be destroyed on that day, O LORD.
verses.31: I am with you, O Lord Yahweh, your army. For your time has come to take action.
verses.32: And when Zadon fell, he could no longer stand. I set fire to his city, and it burned down everything around him.
verses.33: Thus said Jehovah, the God of hosts: “Let the children of Israel and the children of Judah together hold them. And let all those who are with them also hold them in their hands.”
verses.34: May the strong God, the army of Jehovah, reign over them. May they fight against their enemies, so that the land may be at peace, and so that the inhabitants of Babylon may be freed from their troubles.
verses.35: “May the LORD cry out against those who are evil! May He also cry out against the inhabitants of Babylon, against their leaders, and against their wise men.”
verses.36: They destroyed the idols, and they also destroyed their rulers and their leaders.
verses.37: May they be destroyed along with their horses and chariots, and all those things that are inside them. May they become the property of their women, who will then take possession of them.
verses.38: It will be destroyed at its birth, and they will be destroyed because this land is full of destruction. In times of crisis, they will be destroyed.
verses.39: Therefore, the dragons will settle in those islands. They will dwell there forever, and they will never be able to return to their homeland. They will never be able to settle down anywhere else.
verses.40: As God wills, Shem, Amorah, and their inhabitants will be destroyed. The Lord says that no man shall dwell there, nor shall any human being live there.
verses.41: Look, a people has come from the east, and great nations and many kings will be destroyed from the land.
verses.42: Keshet and Kidon will hold Akzari Hema in their hands. They will not show mercy to him. His voice will be like the roar of the sea. They will ride on horses, like warriors ready for battle against you, daughter of Babylon.
verses.43: King Babylon heard their voices, and he trembled with fear as he held the sword in his hand.
verses.44: Look, like a lion, he will rise from the depths of the Jordan River. He will come down to Neva. He will be chosen by me. Who else can stand before him? Who else can compare to him? Who else can guide me? Who is worthy to stand before him?
verses.45: Therefore, listen to the counsel of Jehovah. He has given this advice to Babylon. And consider his thoughts regarding the land of Canaan. If not for the young men who will plow and till it, if not for them who will work on it, then nothing will be done with it.
verses.46: From the sound of Babel’s noise, the earth was made silent. It cried out in the nations, but no one heard it.
